newsitem.title: MEXICO: Bancomer launches mortgage discount plan.
newsitem.headline: Bancomer launches mortgage discount plan.

text.p: Bancomer, Mexico's largest mortgage lender, on Wednesday unveiled a fresh debt-relief program for customers who have stayed current with their home loan payments.
Following the lead of Mexico's largest bank, Banamex, Bancomer will offer a service to qualified customers that could cut their mortgage debts by up to 25 percent in six months, it said.

"From August 1997 to January 1998, as they pay their monthly installments or more, Bancomer will contribute an additional 100 percent of what the client pays. All this goes to capital because Bancomer pays the interest," Victor Borra, the bank's deputy director general for mortgages, said at a news conference.
He said the bank's mortgage programs would cost Bancomer about 1 billion pesos.

The latest scheme would apply only to borrowers whose debts had been converted into inflation-indexed Units of Investment. About 75,000 of the bank's 94,000 mortgage customers are eligble, Borra said.
Currently, Bancomer's mortgage portfolio stands at about 41 billion pesos, or a quarter of the total in the Mexican banking system.

Mortgage holders who have joined Bancomer's previous scheme -- known as Puntos Hipotecarios -- can join the new scheme, with all bonus points accumulated to be applied as a discount on mortgage debts as of August 1997, Borra said.
Mortgage debts skyrocketed in the wake of Mexico's December 1994 peso devaluation, and most banks have offered discount schemes to stem massive default rates.

In June, Banamex launched a mortgage relief plan that grants discounts of up to 25 percent on monthly payments if borrowers have paid their bills for 12 consecutive months. Banamex has said the program will cost 2 billion pesos a year.
Analysts have said the relief plans are likely to cut into bank earnings, even though the costs are expected to be partially offset by a reduction in loan loss provisions.
Bancomer said its program was unique in the banking system because it cut overall debt, not just monthly payments.
